title: Prepare for IELTS in 1 Hour: Step-by-Step Crash Course
exercise: Write the four section timings from memory, then attempt your first official diagnostic.

title: IELTS 2026 Complete 11 Hour Course
exercise: Use the relevant chapters only after your diagnostic reveals a weakness; practise immediately afterwards.

title: IELTS Reading Tips: True False Not Given
exercise: Complete a fresh set of 8–10 TFNG questions; record the sentence proving each True or False answer and the missing information for Not Given.

title: IELTS Reading Strategy: Matching Headings
exercise: Summarise each paragraph in your own short heading before matching the options; record accuracy and time on a fresh passage.

title: Simple Tip for Matching Headings in IELTS Reading
exercise: Apply the tip to three fresh paragraphs and explain why each rejected heading is too broad, too narrow, or unrelated.

title: IELTS Reading Quick Tip: Matching Headings
exercise: Use as a quick reminder before a fresh timed headings set; compare your result with your previous fresh set.

title: IELTS Listening Map Labelling with Alex
exercise: Pause before the explanation and attempt the map; then do a fresh official map task once without replaying.

title: IELTS Listening: Don't Make These 4 Mistakes!
exercise: For your next fresh Listening set, log each changed answer, synonym, negative or similar-sounding distractor that caused a mistake.

title: IELTS Listening: The Marks You're Leaving on the Table
exercise: Classify your latest Listening errors as prediction, distractor, technical accuracy or accent/comprehension, and choose the most frequent category to drill.

title: IELTS Listening Tips: Predicting Answers
exercise: Before a fresh gap-fill recording, label the expected answer type for each gap; listen once and compare prediction with the actual answer.

title: IELTS Listening Part 4: Stop Losing Easy Marks and Increase Your Score
exercise: Complete one fresh Part 4 once; compare every incorrect answer with the transcript and log the exact cause.

title: IELTS Writing Task 1: How to organise your writing
exercise: Take a fresh chart and draft only the introduction, overview and two body paragraph plans, then check that each group has a clear purpose.

title: IELTS Writing Task 1 Introduction Paragraph - High Band Score Lesson
exercise: Write introductions for three fresh charts, preserving subject, unit, location and time period without adding interpretations.

title: Complete Guide to IELTS Academic Writing Task 1
topic: Task 1 overview, charts, maps and processes
exercise: At 05:50 study overviews; at 15:19 maps; at 18:43 diagrams. Write a two-sentence overview and a body plan for one fresh task of each type.

title: How to Plan an IELTS Essay
exercise: Spend 7 minutes planning each of two fresh prompts: identify the exact question, choose a position, and give each body paragraph a main idea plus support.

title: How To Write A Band 9 Task 2 Main Body Paragraph
exercise: Write one paragraph with a clear main idea, explanation and relevant example; revise any sentence that does not develop that idea.

title: IELTS Writing Task 2: How to write an introduction
exercise: Write three short introductions that paraphrase the actual question and state a direct answer; avoid memorised filler.

title: Prepare for IELTS Writing in 1 Hour: Step-by-Step Course
exercise: Work through one original essay using planning, drafting and checking, then save your first draft and revised draft separately.

title: IELTS Speaking Part 1- Dos and Don’ts
exercise: Record answers to six fresh Part 1 questions. Give a direct answer and relevant detail; identify one recurring hesitation or grammar issue.

title: How To Use Your Prep Time for IELTS Speaking Part 2
exercise: Use exactly 60 seconds to make notes for a fresh cue card, then record up to two minutes. Repeat with a different cue card.

title: IELTS Speaking Part 2 Tips
exercise: Record a fresh two-minute cue card response and check organisation, natural continuation and relevant details without memorising a script.

title: 3 Steps to a Band 7+ in IELTS Speaking: Day 3
exercise: Record four abstract follow-up answers. State an opinion, explain why, and develop it with an example or comparison where relevant.
